correctness.rationale: The common quadratic root equation classifies every projective gradient zero, including E1=0. The n−1 gradient quadrics form a complete intersection of projective degree 2^(n−1). On each congruence-one subset two-block restriction is b^2; the corresponding saturated primary components have disjoint degree two each, and their lengths total 2^(n−1), proving equality of saturated ideals. The characteristic-two polar Hessian and anisotropic radical prove each quadratic tangent cone smooth. Exact independent finite instances for n=4,8,12 corroborate but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result provides a natural complete primary decomposition at the non-extremal zero-dimensional boundary of a recently studied singular-locus problem that expressly leaves such components open. It exhibits exponentially many ordinary double points, determines their doubled Jacobian scheme, and gives a complete intersection Hilbert series; the characteristic-two difference between reduced support and scheme length has intrinsic singularity-theoretic value.
